A platform is more than a machine.
▣ Definition
A computer platform is the combination of hardware 
architecture and software environment that allows 
applications to operate.

OS, drivers, libraries, runtime

S SRAM

More expensive
Lower density
Often used for cache

Lower cost per bit

pages.text:
Volatile vs Non-Volatile Memory
Computers need both temporary speed and persistent availability.
Volatile
Data disappears when power is removed.
Examples: registers, cache, RAM.
▥ Non-Volatile
Data remains after power is removed.
Examples: firmware storage, flash, SSD.
◎ ROM / Firmware idea
Some basic instructions must remain available before the operating system loads.

pages.text:
Storage: Persistent Data
Storage keeps applications, files, and system data after power is off.
◉ HDD
Magnetic disk + moving parts
▥ SSD
Flash memory, no moving disk
External / Cloud
Removable or remote persistence
Storage is persistent; RAM is temporary.
